stem:
A 34-year-old woman has double vision and fluctuating weakness that improves after she is given a drug that inhibits acetylcholinesterase.

At her neuromuscular junction, the chemical signal that acts directly on the muscle fiber is which of the following?

options.label: A
options.misconception: A basal-ganglia transmitter is being placed at the muscle junction.
options.explanation: Dopamine acts in central pathways such as the basal nuclei; the neuromuscular junction uses acetylcholine.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The main central excitatory transmitter is being placed at the muscle junction.
options.explanation: Glutamate is excitatory within the central nervous system; skeletal muscle fibers are activated by acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors.

options.label: C
options.text: GABA acting on ligand-gated chloride channels
options.misconception: An inhibitory central transmitter is being placed at the muscle junction.
options.explanation: GABA inhibits neurons in the brain and spinal cord; the junction on the muscle fiber is excitatory and cholinergic.

options.label: D
options.misconception: None; the NMJ transmitter is ACh on the nicotinic receptor of the sarcolemma.
options.explanation: At the neuromuscular junction, the motor neuron's terminals release acetylcholine, which acts on the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor of the sarcolemma; acetylcholinesterase then eliminates it, so inhibiting that enzyme strengthens a weak signal.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A sympathetic transmitter is being placed at the skeletal-muscle junction.
options.explanation: Norepinephrine drives sympathetic effects on the heart and smooth muscle; skeletal muscle is activated by acetylcholine from somatic motor neurons.

context: Learning objective: the NMJ synapse. Presynaptic element: motor neuron terminals; transmitter: acetylcholine; receptor: nicotinic acetylcholine receptor on the sarcolemma; elimination: acetylcholinesterase. Every skeletal muscle fiber is innervated at an NMJ, so drugs that block the esterase boost weak transmission (e.g. myasthenia gravis).
imageCaption: NMJ: ACh vesicles -> nicotinic receptors -> EPP; AChE clears the cleft.
